mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 1.5% signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 1.5%, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is positive over a 5-year period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate a broader economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE increases by > 0.5%, or if the correlation between UNRATE changes and 5-day returns is positive over a 3-year period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances following two consecutive quarters of GDP decline, or if GDP declines are not followed by a significant drop in corporate earnings (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month signals a strong supply-side response, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate higher corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO increases by > 2%, or if the correlation between INDPRO changes and 20-day returns is negative over a 3-year period.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market with strong job growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer spending is expected to rise.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000, or if the combined effect of these conditions on 5-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% in a month signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it indicates a broader economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when HOUST decreases by > 10%, or if the correlation between HOUST changes and 20-day returns is positive over a 3-year period.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1%, it signals inflationary pressure without a corresponding tightening response, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate fiscal stimulus.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% and FEDFUNDS < 1%, or if the combined effect of these conditions on 60-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) over two consecutive months signals strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances following two consecutive months of RSAFS increase, or if RSAFS increases are not followed by a significant rise in corporate earnings (t-test p > 0.05).
